## Argentina, Chile and Colombia: which countries does the journey really include?

**Selecting Argentina, Chile and Colombia in our catalogue means that all three countries appear on the same route, not that the ready-made tour visits only these countries.** The selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. The current programme is [Eight South American Countries in 32 Days: From Rio and Iguazu to the Galapagos and Colombia](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). Its travel dates are 22 October to 22 November 2026.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

The journey begins in Brazil and continues through Argentina, Uruguay, Chile, Bolivia, Peru, Ecuador and Colombia. There is no direct Santiago-to-Medellin flight in this ready-made programme: between them come high-altitude lagoons, Uyuni, Lake Titicaca, Machu Picchu and the Galapagos. These stops determine both the duration and the preparations needed.

| Itinerary stage | When and where |
|---|---|
| Argentina | Days 7–10: Iguazu, Buenos Aires |
| Chile | Days 10–13: Santiago, Atacama |
| Between these stages and Colombia | Bolivia, Peru, Ecuador |
| Colombia | Days 26–32: Medellin, Cartagena, Bogota |

Day 10 includes the flight from Buenos Aires to Santiago, while Day 13 already takes travellers across the Chile–Bolivia border. This is one continuous journey with extensive transfers. If your goal is a holiday limited to the three named countries, the itinerary and duration need to be discussed separately. The [catalogue of all multi-country journeys](/multi-country/) helps compare other combinations, while [Argentina tours](/argentina/tour/), [Chile tours](/chile/tour/) and [Colombia tours](/colombia/tour/) offer options with narrower geographical coverage.

## Argentina: Iguazu, Buenos Aires and a trip to Uruguay

The Argentine stage begins at the Brazilian border. After seeing the Brazilian side of the falls, the group visits the Argentine side near [Puerto Iguazu](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/). On one trip, travellers can compare the panoramic Brazilian views with the trails and viewpoints of Argentina's national park. The border crossing involves distinct immigration procedures; documents and any right of re-entry to Brazil must be considered alongside the flight itinerary.

A flight to [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) follows. The programme includes a city tour with a Russian-speaking guide and an evening tango show with dinner. The next day is devoted to Montevideo: a visit to Uruguay with a return to Argentina. This is especially important when checking the number of entries and transport tickets, as the trip involves crossing an international border in both directions.

In late October, Buenos Aires is in the Southern Hemisphere's spring. Lightweight layers are appropriate for city sightseeing, while Iguazu's wet trails call for comfortable non-slip shoes and rain protection. The same clothes will not keep you comfortable during a night in high-altitude Bolivia several days later.

## Chile: the capital, a flight to Calama and preparation for altitude

On Day 10, the group flies from Buenos Aires to [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/). The following day includes sightseeing in the historic centre and modern districts. A separate visit to Maipo Valley wineries is offered at additional cost. This optional outing is different from the included city tour.

Next, a domestic flight goes to Calama, followed by a transfer to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). The desert lies at altitude, with dry air, intense sunlight and marked differences between daytime and nighttime temperatures. A light jacket, warm mid-layer, sunglasses, hat and water are more useful here than one heavy overcoat.

Day 13 begins a 4×4 crossing of the Bolivian border into the high-altitude lagoons. This is where an urban sightseeing holiday develops physical challenges related to elevation and long hours on the road. Before booking, assess your wellbeing in mountainous conditions, any chronic medical conditions and opportunities for gradual acclimatisation. If you need a different itinerary without Uyuni, compare [tours in Chile](/chile/tour/) and ready-made [Argentina + Chile programmes](/multi-country/argentina_chile/).

### Why you cannot "just add a flight" between Chile and Colombia

The current itinerary travels from Chile into Bolivia, then through Peru to Ecuador. This section covers Days 13–25 and includes [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and the [Galapagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). Removing one stage requires revisiting the sequence of transfers, accommodation and flights. Fewer countries do not automatically produce a proportional reduction in price: airlines, excursions and hotels use different pricing rules.

We help compare possible sequences, coordinate connections and allow reasonable time buffers. On a long journey, transfers before international departures and recovery after high-altitude stages deserve particular attention.

## Colombia: from the Andes to the Caribbean and back to altitude

The Colombian section starts on 16 November with a flight from Ecuador's Guayaquil to [Medellin](/colombia/place/medellin/). The programme includes sightseeing, a journey to [Guatape](/colombia/place/guatape/) and [El Penon Rock](/colombia/place/el-penon-de-guatape/), and a visit to [Comuna 13](/colombia/place/comuna-13/). The group then flies to [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/), which is much hotter and more humid than the mountain cities.

The route ends in [Bogota](/colombia/place/bogota/), with city museums, the viewpoint on Monserrate and a trip to the [Salt Cathedral at Zipaquira](/colombia/place/zipaquira/). Bogota sits high in the Andes, so long trousers and a warm sweater will be useful again even after Cartagena. You will need to change clothes for the weather within a single week, not between seasons.

| City | Distinctive features |
|---|---|
| Medellin | Mountain city, excursions and Guatape |
| Cartagena | Tropical heat on the Caribbean coast |
| Bogota | Cooler because of altitude |

This rapid change of climate zones is a major consideration when packing. A compact set of lightweight quick-drying clothing, a warm mid-layer, a wind- and waterproof jacket and two kinds of footwear is enough for many situations. Walking in cities and on rocky trails calls for different shoes.

## Documents, borders and transit for Russian citizens

For citizens of the Russian Federation travelling on an ordinary international passport, **Argentina, Chile and Colombia have separate short-stay tourist-entry regimes**. Official sources were checked on 16 October 2026. These are three different states, each granting its own permission to enter. A visa or entry stamp from one does not automatically apply in another. The full itinerary also visits Brazil, Uruguay, Bolivia, Peru and Ecuador: requirements must be checked for all eight countries, including repeat entries.

Before buying international tickets, we help prepare a checklist for each traveller's nationality and passport: document validity, confirmed entries, onward tickets, transit-airport restrictions and requirements for children. Rules may be different for other passports. Entry conditions, even under the same visa-waiver agreement, should be checked again immediately before departure.

**Specific considerations for the three countries:**

- **Argentina.** Check documents for entry from Brazil and re-entry after the one-day trip to Uruguay; have evidence of the onward route ready.
- **Chile.** When crossing the border, comply with immigration controls and SAG declarations. Plant and animal products in luggage must be declared according to the service's rules; even snacks, fruit and souvenirs can lead to questions.
- **Colombia.** For arrival by air in Medellin and departure through Bogota, check the advance Check-Mig form and flight details. The official service specifies a submission window from 72 to 1 hour before travel.

Official nationality-based checks matter especially for travellers transiting third countries, using two passports or making extra independent stops. Insurance should cover the complete route, including the high-altitude stages, excursions and Galapagos boat programme. Holding an insurance policy and having the particular activity covered are different things.

## Money: three kinds of peso and expenses in the other countries

Argentina uses **Argentine pesos**, Chile uses **Chilean pesos**, and Colombia uses **Colombian pesos**. Their exchange rates differ, and a price tagged simply "pesos" without a country can lead to budgeting mistakes. US dollars are useful for some tourist payments and exchanges, but not every local purchase can be paid in dollars at a reasonable rate. The complete eight-country itinerary also includes Bolivia with the boliviano, Peru with the sol and Ecuador, whose official currency is the US dollar.

Bank cards require separate planning. Visa and Mastercard cards issued by Russian banks cannot be relied upon abroad following the international payment systems' suspension of operations with Russian banks. Check cards from other issuers, cash options, withdrawal limits and fees individually. Ada Tours can advise at which stages it makes sense to have local cash and a backup payment method, but cannot guarantee that a particular shop or hotel will accept a specific card.

The cost of the extended tour and its included services are given in the [main itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). It specifies 4-star hotels, domestic flights, scheduled transfers and excursions. International flights, optional excursions, tips and meals outside the programme are separate expenses. Check the conditions of optional visits rather than adding the prices of every advertised option together.

## Assessing the pace and alternatives

Thirty-two days make it possible to see many regions, but this is **an active journey with frequent changes of hotels and transportation**. It includes flights, high-altitude 4×4 transfers, boat excursions and major cities. It suits travellers who want to cross a substantial part of the continent in sequence, are prepared for changing weather and are comfortable with busy sightseeing days.

If Patagonia or unhurried time in the mountains is more important, look at [Argentina and Chile itineraries](/multi-country/argentina_chile/). If the Caribbean and Colombian cities are your priority, compare [tours in Colombia](/colombia/tour/) separately. To choose a journey without such a long high-altitude section, Ada Tours first identifies the places you want, an appropriate activity level and the number of days, then proposes a realistic sequence of countries.

## Questions to ask before booking

### Is this a tour only of Argentina, Chile and Colombia?

No. The three countries serve as a catalogue filter. The available 32-day itinerary visits eight countries: Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay, Chile, Bolivia, Peru, Ecuador and Colombia. Dates, excursions and flights are specified in the [complete tour description](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/).

### Can we fly straight from Santiago to Bogota?

Such an option can be considered when tailoring the journey, but it would be a different itinerary. On the published programme, Santiago is followed by Atacama, Bolivia, Peru and Ecuador, while the Colombian section begins in Medellin.

### Where is the greatest challenge from altitude?

The principal high-altitude crossing begins after San Pedro de Atacama and runs through Bolivia's lagoons to Uyuni, La Paz and Peru. Bogota is also at altitude, although a city walk and a multi-day off-road journey impose different demands. Discuss health with a doctor before travel, and the pace and acclimatisation arrangements with the tour specialist.

### Will I need cash if the tour is paid for in advance?

Yes. Cash may be needed for expenses not covered by the programme, tips and personal purchases. Argentina, Chile and Colombia use different local pesos. A backup payment reserve is especially useful on a route with several border crossings.

### How is the journey home arranged?

The final day is in Bogota. The programme includes an onward departure via São Paulo, with a connection to the flight home; the international ticket is paid for separately. Allow enough connection time, taking account of separate tickets, baggage collection and transit rules in Brazil.

## Adventures in three countries: what is actually on the itinerary

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} combining **Argentina, Chile and Colombia** with the adventure theme. In practice, it is an intersection of countries within the [32-day tour through South America](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/): the journey starts in Brazil, visits Argentina and Chile, crosses Bolivia, Peru and Ecuador, and finishes in Colombia. The three selected countries make up only part of the complete route.

Activities vary in intensity. The Argentine side of Iguazu includes a national-park excursion. In Chile, travellers arrive at San Pedro de Atacama before a high-altitude crossing. In Colombia, the itinerary visits El Penol and Guatape. However, the main 4×4 route takes place **in Bolivia**, and the programme does not describe professional climbing, technical canyoning or multi-day trekking in the three selected countries.

Compare the actual days, elevations, transfer times and level of exertion. If the combination of countries matters more than the theme, use the [general Argentina + Chile + Colombia catalogue](/multi-country/argentina_chile_colombia/). Other active-travel options are gathered in the [multi-country adventure catalogue](/multi-country/interests/adventure/).

## Argentina: Iguazu nature trails and urban sightseeing

The Argentine section introduces [Puerto Iguazu](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) and its national park. Humid subtropical forest surrounds the waterfalls, which are viewed from the park's open tourist routes. For a nature lover, this is a chance to approach the river's cascades and see the scenery from the other side of the border compared with Brazil.

**The usual Iguazu sightseeing excursion is not an extreme river descent or a sporting trek.** On this itinerary, the Argentine side is visited on a group excursion with a Russian-speaking guide, followed by a flight to Buenos Aires. A separate [Macuco Safari on the Brazilian side](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) is mentioned as an extra paid option and should not be counted as included exertion or as part of the basic price.

In [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), travellers then enjoy city routes and a tango show. The focus shifts from nature to architecture and culture. Rest between long transfers matters just as much as additional walks: the schedule of an extended journey does not mean every free evening can be used as a full separate sightseeing day.

## Chile: from Santiago to the dry Atacama

The Chilean stage begins in [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), followed by a flight via Calama to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). This desert oasis serves as the base for preparing to cross the high-altitude region. Chile's national tourism service presents Atacama as a destination for desert scenery, astronomy and mountain experiences. However, the range of possible regional activities is broader than what this particular tour actually includes.

On this programme, San Pedro de Atacama is **an acclimatisation stop before Bolivia**. An evening astronomy excursion to telescopes is available separately, depending in part on observing conditions and the lunar calendar. The existence of the option does not make it an obligatory evening activity.

The next day begins a two-day 4×4 route through Bolivia's highlands, lagoons and salt flats. This is the most prominent off-road stage of the entire journey. It calls for tolerance of long periods on uneven roads, temperature changes and significant altitude. Anyone choosing primarily for Atacama should distinguish time spent **in Chile** from time spent in neighbouring **Bolivia**: attractive photographs of both regions do not imply identical routes, transport or overnight conditions.

For more active trips involving Chile, see the [Chile adventure selection](/interests/adventure/tours/chile/).

## Colombia: El Penon Rock, Guatape and urban Medellin

After Ecuador, the programme reaches [Medellin](/colombia/place/medellin/). From here, a visit is scheduled to El Penol, El Penon Rock and [Guatape](/colombia/place/guatape/). Travellers learn about the history of a relocated settlement, see reservoir views and Guatape's painted facades. The excursion lasts **eight hours**, including road travel.

El Penon is a distinctive rock rising above the lake landscape. However, climbing its stairs to the summit is not guaranteed for every traveller: **visiting the rock and undertaking the climb are different conditions**. If the ascent is essential to you, confirm access, your health requirements and the time allowed for the stop.

The itinerary then includes sightseeing in Medellin with Comuna 13, a flight to [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/), a historical programme on the Caribbean coast, and [Bogota](/colombia/place/bogota/) with Zipaquira. These stops enrich the journey but chiefly concern urban history and culture. They are city and cultural excursions; the overall length of the trip does not turn them into sporting adventures.

## The main demands: how much activity and where to be careful

| Stage | Actual demands |
|---|---|
| Argentina | Walks at Iguazu, flights |
| Chile | Flight and adjustment to altitude |
| Bolivia | Two days in 4×4 vehicles |
| Colombia | A long excursion to Guatape |

**Altitude is a separate concern.** Conditions change significantly between San Pedro de Atacama and Bolivia's high-altitude lagoons. The itinerary includes an acclimatisation stop, but it does not guarantee freedom from altitude sickness. Travellers with cardiovascular, respiratory or other significant health concerns need medical advice beforehand. Evaluate physical demands across every stage, including Bolivia and Peru, not only the three countries in this page's title.

Practical points to discuss before departure include the length of the dirt-road journeys, overnight elevations, opportunities to rest, baggage limits on domestic flights, and clothing for hot lowlands and cold highlands. The correct packing list depends on the dates and sequence of the specific itinerary. Entry rules should also be checked for all eight countries, not just Argentina, Chile and Colombia: requirements depend on nationality and need current official verification.

The exact itinerary, flight arrangements and included excursions are available on the current programme page:

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

## Who this combination suits

This option appeals to travellers who enjoy **a mixed format**: striking natural sites, long international transfers, urban sightseeing and one separate off-road stage. It serves a different purpose from a programme for someone who wants to hike demanding mountain trails or do technical sports every day.

If Atacama and Bolivia are your priorities, compare [Chile adventure tours](/interests/adventure/tours/chile/) with other multi-country itineraries. If Colombia and walks around Guatape matter more, decide how long you want to spend there rather than assume there is a free day when the schedule actually includes a flight.

## Frequently asked questions about adventures in Argentina, Chile and Colombia

### Is there genuine off-road driving on the tour?

Yes. A two-day 4×4 journey takes place in the high-altitude section **of Bolivia** after Chilean Atacama. It is part of the full eight-country itinerary, although Bolivia is not named in this three-country filter.

### Will I need mountaineering experience?

No specialised ascent or multi-day mountaineering route is listed in the published programme. The main activities are sightseeing walks, road transfers and a 4×4 excursion.

### Do I have to climb to the summit of El Penon?

The published excursion description does not establish this as compulsory. The itinerary includes visiting the rock and Guatape area; opportunities to climb should be confirmed separately.

### Can someone without high-altitude experience join the trip?

No experience with technical trekking is specified, but Bolivia's high-altitude stages call for serious attention to wellbeing. Anyone with significant medical limitations should discuss the journey with a doctor and check overnight stops, transfers and rest options in advance.

### Are the three countries visited consecutively?

No. The [32-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) includes other countries and lengthy stages between them. The catalogue selection means each named country is on the route, not that they border one another or are visited consecutively.

## Three countries, three perspectives on South American history

Argentina, Chile and Colombia are especially interesting together because visitors discover different sides of the continent's urban history. In [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), historic neighbourhoods, squares and tango are central. In [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), the old administrative centre and neighbourhoods at the foot of the Andes take the spotlight. In [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/) and [Bogota](/colombia/place/bogota/), visitors encounter colonial heritage, museum collections and cultural changes of recent decades.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with all three countries on the principal itinerary and "Culture and History" among the themes. The current programme is the [32-day journey through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). Besides Argentina, Chile and Colombia, it visits Brazil, Uruguay, Bolivia, Peru and Ecuador.

**This is a thematic intersection of a long itinerary, not a separate tour of only three countries.** Between Santiago and Colombia, the journey crosses Bolivia's highlands, Inca monuments in Peru and the Galapagos, so the duration is determined by the entire sequence of stops.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

## Argentina: Buenos Aires, historic neighbourhoods and tango

After visiting the Argentine side of Iguazu Falls, travellers fly to Buenos Aires. A city tour introduces several distinct neighbourhoods of the capital. [La Boca](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) and San Telmo reveal the life of older districts, while Plaza de Mayo and its surroundings present the city's political and administrative centre.

It is particularly worthwhile to consider these places together. Buenos Aires unfolds through the connections between port history, immigrant culture, old squares and the modern capital. A walk in Recoleta adds another architectural environment.

An **evening tango show with dinner** is scheduled. Tango is part of discovering the city, not a vague optional suggestion to "go to a concert": the evening really is included in the published tour programme. For travellers selecting a trip for cultural reasons, that is an important difference from an ordinary transit stop in the capital.

The Argentine section also visits Iguazu Falls. That is the natural part of the longer journey; for the culture-and-history theme, Buenos Aires is the main focus.

## Chile: Santiago and urban history beside the Andes

After Buenos Aires, the itinerary reaches Santiago by air. A city tour with a Russian-speaking guide visits several important sights. One central stop is [La Moneda Palace](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), originally built as a mint and later becoming a major government building in Chile.

The tour continues to Plaza de Armas, surrounded by historic administrative and religious buildings. Going up Santa Lucia Hill provides views across Santiago's development, while travelling through the modern districts of Vitacura, Las Condes and Providencia shows how the city expanded beyond the old centre.

This is particularly suitable for travellers interested in **the transition from a colonial city to a modern capital**. The architecture and purposes of particular buildings connect to the country's history. The excursion involves more than a photograph in the main square.

After Santiago, the journey moves into Atacama and then Bolivia. There is no separate multi-day historical expedition in Chile: the section consists of city sightseeing, a flight to Calama and the continuation of the wider journey. Maipo Valley wineries are offered separately for an additional charge and should not be counted as an automatically included cultural day.

## Colombia: from Medellin to colonial Cartagena

Travellers arrive in Colombia after Ecuador. The first major stop is [Medellin](/colombia/place/medellin/). The programme combines a visit to the Guatape area with a later city tour, including [Comuna 13](/colombia/place/comuna-13/), where contemporary urban culture is closely connected to the history of social change.

Visiting Comuna 13 helps show Colombia beyond old cathedrals and museum displays. Contemporary forms of city life, public spaces and local stories matter on a cultural journey too. The detailed stops are determined by the actual excursion, however, not by any famous site in Medellin.

The next stop is **Cartagena**, a historic port on the Caribbean coast. The sightseeing excursion includes views over the bay, the old city, the Manga neighbourhood, San Felipe de Barajas Fortress and a walk along historic streets past San Pedro Claver Church. The fortification walls and military architecture show why the defence of a Caribbean port was so significant in the colonial period.

Cartagena's historic fortified centre is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Yet the city is also rewarding beyond individual monuments: its squares, facades and narrow streets allow visitors to spend several hours immersed in an old urban environment.

## Bogota: pre-Columbian heritage, art and the Salt Cathedral

After Cartagena, the itinerary flies to [Bogota](/colombia/place/bogota/). Here the transition between colonial architecture and the history of peoples who inhabited the Andes before the Spanish conquest is especially apparent.

The published programme includes La Candelaria's historic centre, the **Gold Museum**, the Botero Collection and the Casa de Moneda. The excursion also visits Bolivar Square and Monserrate. In the museums, visitors can compare objects from pre-Columbian cultures with later works of art.

The days on which museums open matter: the programme specifically notes that the Gold Museum is closed on Mondays, while the Casa de Moneda and Botero Collection are closed on Tuesdays. Check the excursion order and actual opening status for the travel date.

A separate trip to the [Zipaquira Salt Cathedral](/colombia/place/zipaquira/) and a visit inside the cathedral are then scheduled. This is another unusual cultural site beyond the capital, quite different from Bogota's museums and Cartagena's old fortifications.

## What connects the cultural days in the three countries

The ready-made programme allows travellers to compare how capital squares developed in different South American countries, how port neighbourhoods took shape, how art changed and how historical heritage was preserved. Each stop has its own focus.

| City | Cultural stops and their significance |
|---|---|
| Buenos Aires | San Telmo, La Boca, Plaza de Mayo and tango: neighbourhood history and traditions |
| Santiago | La Moneda, Plaza de Armas, Santa Lucia: old centre and modern capital |
| Medellin | Comuna 13: contemporary urban history |
| Cartagena | Old Town, San Felipe and San Pedro Claver: colonial port heritage |
| Bogota and Zipaquira | Gold Museum, Botero Collection and Salt Cathedral: ancient cultures and art |

The cultural part of the wider tour does not end there. Between Chile and Colombia, travellers visit Tiwanaku in Bolivia, Cusco and Machu Picchu in Peru, and historic Quito in Ecuador. **But those sites lie outside Argentina, Chile and Colombia**. They belong to the extended eight-country programme and must not be attributed to the selected three countries.

## Choosing the length of a cultural journey

If you can spend 32 days travelling and want to explore the history of several regions, the ready-made eight-country itinerary includes all the cultural stops mentioned. It also contains many flights and nature excursions, so not every free minute can be devoted to museums.

For a trip focused on Argentina, Chile and Colombia alone, first establish priorities: is one Santiago city excursion enough, how many days would you like in Buenos Aires, and is Cartagena or Bogota's museums more important to you in Colombia? A bespoke itinerary can then be arranged without the need to cross Bolivia, Peru and Ecuador.

The [Argentina, Chile and Colombia catalogue](/multi-country/argentina_chile_colombia/) shows all journeys involving these countries. For other cultural programmes, see [multi-country culture and history tours](/multi-country/interests/culture-and-history/) and the broader [Culture and History](/interests/culture-and-history/) section.

## Frequently asked questions about cultural travel in Argentina, Chile and Colombia

### Is there a ready-made programme covering only these three countries?

The current thematic selection contains a 32-day tour through eight countries. It includes Argentina, Chile and Colombia, but also travels through Brazil, Uruguay, Bolivia, Peru and Ecuador.

### Is tango in Buenos Aires included?

Yes. The current itinerary includes a tango show with dinner. The exact arrangements are specified in the selected tour.

### Which historical sites are visited in Santiago?

The city tour covers central Santiago, La Moneda Palace, Plaza de Armas, Santa Lucia Hill and the modern districts.

### Where are the main colonial sights in Colombia?

Cartagena has a particularly extensive colonial programme on this tour: its historic centre, fortifications and San Felipe Fortress. In Bogota, the focus also includes museums, art and pre-Columbian history.

### Are the Gold Museum and the Botero Collection included?

Both are named in the Bogota tour programme. Museums have regular closing days, however, so check visits against the exact travel calendar.

### Can I spend more time in museums and shorten the nature days?

That requires separate bespoke planning. The ready-made 32-day itinerary has an agreed sequence of nature and cultural stops; a different balance of days needs to be arranged individually.

## Waterfalls, high-altitude desert and green hills: three South American landscapes

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} and corresponds to the [32-day journey through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). [Argentina](/argentina/), [Chile](/chile/) and [Colombia](/colombia/) are part of the principal route, alongside Brazil, Uruguay, Bolivia, Peru and Ecuador.

This is **not a specialised three-country expedition**. The tour begins in Brazil and ends after the Colombian stage. The key question for nature lovers is which natural sites are actually visited and where a stop consists only of a panorama, a city excursion or a transfer. For all options involving these countries, visit the [Argentina, Chile and Colombia combination catalogue](/multi-country/argentina_chile_colombia/).

## Argentina: Iguazu Falls, not Patagonia

Argentina's natural stage follows the Brazilian side of [Iguazu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). Travellers cross to [Puerto Iguazu](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) and visit the Argentine side of the falls with a Russian-speaking guide in a group. The wide panoramas from Brazil are complemented by other accessible viewpoints of the cascades.

UNESCO recognises Argentina's Iguazu National Park as a natural World Heritage site, including its surviving subtropical Atlantic Forest. It is a protected ecosystem, but the included excursion is primarily about the falls. Encounters with particular animal species are not guaranteed.

After Iguazu, the route becomes urban, with [Buenos Aires](/argentina/) sightseeing and a tango show. **Patagonia, El Calafate, Perito Moreno and Ushuaia are not scheduled on this itinerary.** Travellers chiefly interested in Argentina's glaciers and mountain trails need a different programme, rather than assume those places are included because the catalogue carries a "Nature" label.

## Chile: Santiago and the approach to Atacama

Chile begins with a city tour in [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/). A flight to Calama and transfer to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) follow. This town is the starting point for the high-altitude section and an acclimatisation stop before reaching the Bolivian border.

### Where Chilean nature ends and Bolivian nature begins

The most substantial nature experiences after San Pedro occur on a 4×4 route through **Bolivian** lagoons and salt flats. They include [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/), [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/) and the [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) area. Although the section begins in Chile, describing all these places as Chilean would be factually wrong.

An evening astronomy excursion in Atacama is also offered separately on this programme. It is **optional**; price and availability are agreed individually, including consideration of the lunar calendar. The desert's observing potential must not be turned into an included telescope night without confirmation.

The altitude stage imposes particular demands on wellbeing. The source itinerary includes acclimatisation in San Pedro de Atacama and identifies a risk of altitude sickness in Bolivia. Account for the elevation, dry air, temperature changes and actual driving conditions on the 4×4 route.

## Colombia: El Penon Rock, reservoirs and mountain views

The Colombian section begins in [Medellin](/colombia/place/medellin/). Travellers then visit [El Penon de Guatape Rock](/colombia/place/el-penon-de-guatape/) and [Guatape](/colombia/place/guatape/). Reservoir views, rolling hills and excursion stops are the main attractions. An English-speaking guide is provided; the excursion's title does not imply technical climbing or an independent mountain hike.

The following days visit Cartagena and Bogota. In the capital, the route includes [Monserrate](/colombia/place/monserrate-bogota/), a hill above the city offering panoramic views. However, **an Amazon expedition, wildlife watching in a nature reserve or a separate Colombian jungle trip are not listed**. Colombia's nature component centres on mountain and water landscapes visible around the actual city-excursion stops.

## Where to find wildlife on a journey through Argentina, Chile and Colombia

Argentina, Chile and Colombia have very different landscapes, but **not every nature stop on this specific Ada Tours itinerary involves watching animals**. On the Argentine stage, trails pass through humid forest near Iguazu Falls. Chile leads towards the dry high-altitude Atacama. In Colombia, the itinerary includes hills and reservoirs around Guatape, although most time is spent on urban excursions.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} featuring the three selected countries and the "Wildlife and Safaris" theme. It contains the [32-day Eight Countries of South America tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). The principal geography also includes Brazil, Uruguay, Bolivia, Peru and Ecuador. **Filtering for Argentina, Chile and Colombia does not mean a separate direct route exists between those three countries.**

## Argentina: close to Iguazu Falls

The Argentine section begins near [Puerto Iguazu](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/). Travellers visit the national park and approach the waterfalls along maintained walkways. Forest lies close by: humid air, dense vegetation and the sound of rushing water create conditions sharply different from the high-altitude stages that follow.

The national park protects areas of Atlantic Forest inhabited by birds and mammals. However, the organised excursion focuses on the waterfalls, viewpoints and forest environment. A sighting of a particular wild animal is not guaranteed. Dedicated birdwatching with a specialist guide would need to be agreed as a separate format.

On this tour, Argentine Iguazu follows immediately after the Brazilian side. Nearby [Foz do Iguacu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) offers wider panoramas. Although Argentina is selected in the filter, **the Brazilian national park is a real part of the same programme**, not an optional extra added to a three-country trip.

Travellers then continue to [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), where historic neighbourhood walks and tango belong to the cultural, rather than natural, side of the itinerary.

## Chile: Atacama Desert and the approach to the highlands

After flying from Buenos Aires to Santiago, the itinerary continues through Calama to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). Desert expanses, mountains and volcanic scenery surround it. This is a memorable nature stage, particularly for visitors interested in open landscapes and Andean geography.

**The published itinerary does not list a dedicated wildlife-watching excursion on the Chilean stage.** The next day the route crosses into Bolivia, where the 4×4 journey through high-altitude lagoons begins, including Laguna Colorada, home to flamingos.

The national distinction matters. Flamingos and the lakes of Bolivia's Altiplano are genuine experiences on the eight-country tour, but should not be attributed to Chilean stops. If your objective is birds on high-altitude lakes, look first at the Bolivian section and the time allotted to the [lagoons and Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), then consider how long you spend in Atacama.

A night in San Pedro de Atacama also helps prepare for the subsequent climb in altitude. Conditions in the highlands are very different from Iguazu: low temperatures, dry air and possible reactions to altitude need separate preparation.

## Colombia: Guatape and the green mountains

The Colombian section begins after Ecuador. Travellers fly from Guayaquil to [Medellin](/colombia/place/medellin/), then head for [Guatape](/colombia/place/guatape/) and [El Penon de Guatape Rock](/colombia/place/el-penon-de-guatape/). Green hills and winding reservoir shores can be seen here. The programme includes a full-day excursion to these places.

For scenery lovers, the day contrasts vividly with dry Atacama. However, the trip is arranged as sightseeing around the landscape and settlements, not as a specialised safari or birdwatching expedition. Climbing the rock and any extra activities must be assessed against the specific excursion terms; a picture of a mountain landscape does not by itself establish that they are included.

The remaining Colombian days visit [Comuna 13](/colombia/place/comuna-13/) in Medellin, the historic streets of [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/), [Bogota](/colombia/place/bogota/) and the Salt Cathedral at Zipaquira. This is a rich cultural programme. When choosing Colombia for nature, be clear about the actual offer: on this itinerary, the main scenic stop is the Guatape area.

## Where most wildlife watching really takes place

The complete active tour has the "Wildlife and Safaris" theme because of encounters at Bolivia's lagoons and the Galapagos, outside the three selected countries. Scenic stops also belong to the separate "Nature" theme. Consider the full itinerary:

| Stage | Nature and activity format |
|---|---|
| Argentina, Iguazu | Waterfalls and forest; wildlife sightings possible but not guaranteed |
| Chile, Atacama | Desert and mountains; no dedicated wildlife excursion |
| Bolivia, lagoons | High-altitude lakes with flamingo habitats |
| Ecuador, Galapagos | Boat excursion and island fauna; one of two routes |
| Colombia, Guatape | Rock and reservoir; sightseeing, not safari |

In Ecuador, the [Galapagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/) programme includes a boat excursion following **one of two alternatives**, confirmed after booking. North Seymour with Bachas beaches and South Plaza with Cape Carrion are different versions of one day. Encounters with frigatebirds, boobies, sea lions and iguanas depend on the selected stop and natural conditions.

For nature enthusiasts, the eight-country journey therefore offers a combination of several ecosystems. But anyone wanting to focus strictly on Argentina, Chile and Colombia would need to select additional nature excursions in those countries separately. The ready-made tour does not automatically include specialist animal-watching outings in each country.

Atacama offers the contrast of desert mountains and highlands. Guatape offers reservoir views. If you particularly want the islands' endemic animals, focus more attention on the Galapagos stage, which takes place in another country.

## Frequently asked questions about nature in Argentina, Chile and Colombia

### Is there a tour of only the three selected countries?

No. The current 32-day itinerary visits eight South American countries. Argentina, Chile and Colombia are three principal countries among eight, not a standalone three-country programme.

### Where can I see wildlife on the Argentine stage?

The most relevant place is Iguazu National Park and its protected Atlantic Forest. The waterfall excursion is included, but sightings of particular animal species are not promised.

### Are the flamingos part of the Chile excursions?

On this tour, the high-altitude lagoons with flamingos lie in Bolivia, after crossing the border from Chile. These two stages must not be confused.

### Is a safari scheduled in Colombia?

No. The published itinerary's Colombian nature stop is the Guatape and El Penon Rock excursion. There is no specialist safari or birdwatching outing in this section.

### Are both Galapagos boat-excursion routes included?

No. The programme offers one of the alternative island routes, with the option confirmed after booking.

### Do I need to prepare for altitude if my main interest is nature?

Yes, if you choose the complete eight-country tour: between Chile and Colombia it passes through high-altitude Bolivia, Peru and Quito. Assess physical demands in advance in light of your health.
